---

## CC91 -- Forum System (Full-Stack)

### 1. What Is This Project?

CC91 is a **university campus forum system** (modeled after CC98, a well-known Zhejiang University BBS). It is a full-stack web application with a Spring Boot backend and React frontend. The project name in the repo is "LargeScale" and the code lives under the `com.cc91` package. The CLAUDE.md file is written in Chinese and describes output formatting preferences (preferring HTML over Markdown for reports).

**Key project files:**
- `D:/aToys/LargeScale/README.md` -- main documentation
- `D:/aToys/LargeScale/CLAUDE.md` -- agent instructions
- `D:/aToys/LargeScale/.env.example` -- environment template
- `D:/aToys/LargeScale/docs/architecture.md` -- architecture spec
- `D:/aToys/LargeScale/docs/issues.md` -- issue tracker

---

### 2. Overall Directory Structure

```
D:\aToys\LargeScale\
  .claude/             -- Claude Code skills (vercel-react-best-practices)
  .vscode/             -- VS Code settings
  backend/             -- Spring Boot 3.2 Java backend
    pom.xml
    src/main/java/com/cc91/
      config/          -- 5 config classes (Security, CORS, Web, ExceptionHandler, DevDataInit)
      controller/      -- 8 REST controllers
      dto/             -- 22 DTOs
      entity/          -- 8 JPA entities
      exception/       -- 3 custom exceptions
      repository/      -- 8 Spring Data JPA repositories
      security/        -- JWT filter, JwtUtil, UserDetailsService
      service/         -- 6 service classes
    src/main/resources/
      application.yml, application-dev.yml
      db/migration/    -- 8 Flyway SQL migrations (V1 through V8)
    src/test/java/     -- 14 test classes (8 controller + 6 service tests)
  frontend/            -- React 19 + Vite + TypeScript
    package.json
    vite.config.ts
    src/
      api/             -- 8 API modules + mockDb + types
      components/      -- 15 reusable components
      context/         -- AuthContext
      hooks/           -- useDebounce
      lib/             -- queryClient, queryKeys
      pages/           -- 17 page components
      pages/admin/     -- 4 admin page components
      __tests__/       -- 20 test files (4 component + 16 page tests)
      test/            -- test setup and utilities
      utils/           -- formatDate
      assets/          -- images (banner, avatars)
  docs/                -- architecture.md, issues.md
```

---

### 3. Frontend Analysis

**Tech stack (all confirmed in `package.json`):**
- React 19.2.4, React DOM 19.2.4
- react-router-dom 7.14.0 (routing)
- @tanstack/react-query 5.99.0 (server state management)
- Axios 1.15.0 (HTTP client)
- Vite 8.0.4 (build tool)
- TypeScript 6.0.2
- Vitest 4.1.4 + React Testing Library 16.3.2 (testing)
- Coverage: @vitest/coverage-v8

**Routing setup (from `D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/App.tsx`):**

The app uses `BrowserRouter` with nested routes. A `Layout` component wraps public-facing pages with Header/Footer. Admin pages use a separate `AdminLayout`.

| Route | Page | Auth Required |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | HomePage | No |
| `/login` | LoginPage | No |
| `/register` | RegisterPage | No |
| `/forgot-password` | ForgotPasswordPage | No |
| `/reset-password` | ResetPasswordPage | No |
| `/profile/:username` | ProfilePage | No |
| `/profile/edit` | ProfileEditPage | Yes |
| `/dashboard` | DashboardPage | Yes |
| `/dashboard/posts` | MyPostsPage | Yes |
| `/dashboard/comments` | MyCommentsPage | Yes |
| `/dashboard/drafts` | MyDraftsPage | Yes |
| `/posts` | PostListPage | No |
| `/posts/:id` | PostDetailPage | No |
| `/posts/new` | CreatePostPage | Yes |
| `/posts/:id/edit` | EditPostPage | Yes |
| `/category/:id` | CategoryPage | No |
| `/search` | SearchPage | No |
| `/notifications` | NotificationsPage | Yes |
| `/admin` | AdminDashboard | Admin |
| `/admin/categories` | CategoryManage | Admin |
| `/admin/content` | ContentModeration | Admin |
| `/admin/users` | UserManage | Admin |
| `*` | NotFoundPage | No |

**Components (15 files in `src/components/`):**
- Header, Footer, Layout, AdminLayout -- structural
- BoardCard, PostCard, TopicTable -- content display
- CommentSection -- comment thread rendering
- NotificationBell -- unread count badge
- Pagination, Breadcrumbs -- navigation aids
- ProtectedRoute, AdminRoute -- auth guards
- ErrorBoundary, ErrorMessage -- error handling
- SafeLink, AnnouncementPanel, MockBanner -- utilities

**Notable frontend feature -- Mock mode:**
`D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/api/mockDb.ts` is a comprehensive 875-line client-side mock database that runs in localStorage. When the backend is unreachable (network error), the frontend automatically falls back to mock mode. The mock implements all API endpoints with realistic seed data (4 categories, 8 posts, 9 comments, 3 users, notifications). This allows the frontend to be developed and demonstrated independently of the backend.

**State management:**
- `AuthContext` in `D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx` -- stores user, isAuthenticated, isAdmin in React context + localStorage
- `@tanstack/react-query` -- all server data fetching goes through React Query with centralized query keys (`D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/lib/queryKeys.ts`)
- JWT tokens stored in localStorage with automatic refresh interceptor in the Axios client

**Theming:**
The Layout supports 4 themes (classic blue, warm tea, sakura pink, dark) toggled via a paint-brush button in the Header. Theme classes are applied to the body element.

---

### 4. Backend Analysis

**Tech stack (from `D:/aToys/LargeScale/backend/pom.xml`):**
- Spring Boot 3.2.0 (parent)
- Spring Security (JWT stateless auth)
- Spring Data JPA / Hibernate
- MySQL 8.0+ (production), H2 (test)
- Flyway (8 database migrations)
- jjwt 0.12.3 (JWT library)
- Lombok (optional)
- spring-dotenv 4.0.0 (.env file support)
- JUnit 5 + MockMvc + Mockito (testing)

**API Endpoints (from controllers in `D:/aToys/LargeScale/backend/src/main/java/com/cc91/controller/`):**

Auth (`/api/auth`):
- `POST /api/auth/register` -- Register
- `POST /api/auth/verify-email` -- Verify email
- `POST /api/auth/login` -- Login (returns JWT + refresh token)
- `POST /api/auth/refresh` -- Refresh tokens
- `POST /api/auth/logout` -- Invalidate refresh token
- `POST /api/auth/forgot-password` -- Send reset code
- `POST /api/auth/reset-password` -- Reset password
- `GET /api/auth/health` -- Health check

Users (`/api/users`):
- `GET /api/users/me` -- Current user profile
- `GET /api/users/{username}` -- View any user profile
- `PUT /api/users/me/profile` -- Update profile
- `GET /api/users/me/posts` -- My posts
- `GET /api/users/me/drafts` -- My drafts
- `GET /api/users/me/comments` -- My comments
- `PUT /api/users/me/password` -- Change password

Posts (`/api/posts`):
- `GET /api/posts` -- Paginated post list (with status filter)
- `GET /api/posts/{id}` -- Post detail (increments view count)
- `GET /api/posts/by-category/{categoryId}` -- Posts by category
- `GET /api/posts/search` -- Search by keyword
- `POST /api/posts` -- Create post
- `PUT /api/posts/{id}` -- Update post
- `DELETE /api/posts/{id}` -- Delete post

Comments (`/api`):
- `GET /api/posts/{postId}/comments` -- Comments for a post
- `POST /api/posts/{postId}/comments` -- Create comment
- `POST /api/comments/{id}/reply` -- Reply to comment
- `DELETE /api/comments/{id}` -- Delete comment

Categories (`/api/categories`):
- `GET /api/categories` -- All categories
- `GET /api/categories/{id}` -- Category detail
- `POST /api/categories` -- Create (admin only)
- `PUT /api/categories/{id}` -- Update (admin only)
- `DELETE /api/categories/{id}` -- Delete (admin only)

Notifications (`/api/notifications`):
- `GET /api/notifications` -- List notifications
- `GET /api/notifications/unread-count` -- Unread count
- `PUT /api/notifications/{id}/read` -- Mark as read
- `PUT /api/notifications/read-all` -- Mark all as read

Admin (`/api/admin`):
- `GET /api/admin/posts` -- All posts (status filter)
- `PUT /api/admin/posts/{id}/status` -- Change post status
- `DELETE /api/admin/posts/{id}` -- Force delete post
- `GET /api/admin/comments` -- All comments
- `DELETE /api/admin/comments/{id}` -- Force delete comment
- `GET /api/admin/users` -- User list (paginated)
- `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/ban` -- Ban user
- `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/unban` -- Unban user
- `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/role` -- Change user role

**Database Entities (8 JPA entities in `D:/aToys/LargeScale/backend/src/main/java/com/cc91/entity/`):**
- `User` -- id, username, email, passwordHash, role (USER/ADMIN), isLocked, failedLoginAttempts, lockUntil, profile (OneToOne)
- `UserProfile` -- userId, avatarUrl, bio, location, website
- `Post` -- id, title, content, authorId, categoryId, viewCount, status (PUBLISHED/DRAFT/DELETED), author/category (ManyToMany)
- `Comment` -- id, postId, authorId, content, parentId, status, parent/replies (self-referential tree)
- `Category` -- id, name, description, sortOrder
- `Notification` -- id, userId, type, title, content, relatedId, isRead
- `RefreshToken` -- id, userId, token, expiresAt, revoked
- `VerificationCode` -- id, email, code, type, expiresAt, used

**Database migrations (8 Flyway scripts in `D:/aToys/LargeScale/backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/`):**
- V1: Initial schema (users, verification_codes, refresh_tokens) with test data
- V2: User profiles table
- V3: Posts table
- V4: Comments table
- V5: Categories table
- V6: Add category_id to posts
- V7: Notifications table
- V8: Add role column to users

**Security configuration (`D:/aToys/LargeScale/backend/src/main/java/com/cc91/config/SecurityConfig.java`):**
- Stateless JWT sessions, CSRF disabled
- CORS configured from env variables
- Public endpoints: `/api/auth/**`, GET on posts/categories/user profiles
- Admin endpoints: `hasRole('ADMIN')` via `@PreAuthorize`
- BCrypt password encoding
- Account lockout after 5 failed attempts (configurable)

---

### 5. Docker / Deployment

**There is NO Docker configuration.** No Dockerfile, no docker-compose.yml, no .dockerignore was found anywhere in the project. Deployment is manual:
- Backend: `mvn spring-boot:run` on port 8080
- Frontend: `npm run dev` (Vite dev server) on port 5173
- Production build exists at `D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/dist/` (pre-built)

---

### 6. Test Coverage

**Backend tests (14 test files in `D:/aToys/LargeScale/backend/src/test/java/com/cc91/`):**

Controller tests (8):
- AuthControllerTest, CategoryControllerTest, CommentControllerTest, NotificationControllerTest, PostControllerTest, UserControllerTest, AdminContentControllerTest, AdminUserControllerTest

Service tests (6):
- AuthServiceTest, CategoryServiceTest, CommentServiceTest, NotificationServiceTest, PostServiceTest, UserServiceTest

Tests use H2 in-memory database (`jdbc:h2:mem`), MockMvc for controller integration tests, and `@SpringBootTest` with Flyway disabled. There is a test-specific config at `D:/aToys/LargeScale/backend/src/test/resources/application-test.yml`.

**Frontend tests (20 test files in `D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/__tests__/`):**

Component tests (4):
- CommentSection.test.tsx, NotificationBell.test.tsx, ProtectedRoute.test.tsx, AuthContext.test.tsx

Page tests (16):
- HomePage, LoginPage, RegisterPage, DashboardPage, MyPostsPage, MyCommentsPage, MyDraftsPage, ProfilePage, ProfileEditPage, PostListPage, PostDetailPage, CreatePostPage, EditPostPage, CategoryPage, SearchPage, NotificationsPage, ForgotPasswordPage, ResetPasswordPage, NotFoundPage

Tests use Vitest + React Testing Library with mocked API calls and localStorage. A previous coverage report exists at `D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/coverage/` (HTML reports generated).

---

### 7. Implementation Status Summary

**Fully implemented (working end-to-end):**
- User authentication (register, login, JWT, refresh, forgot/reset password)
- User profiles (view, edit)
- Posts (CRUD, drafts, pagination, status management)
- Comments (create, reply, threaded tree, delete)
- Categories (CRUD, admin-only management)
- Search (keyword-based post search)
- Notifications (create, list, read/unread, bell indicator)
- Admin dashboard (user management, content moderation, category management)
- Mock mode (full frontend works without backend)

**Known incomplete items (from `D:/aToys/LargeScale/docs/issues.md`):**
- F-02: Admin comment moderation UI -- `adminDeleteComment` API exists but the UI for reviewing comments in ContentModeration is not complete
- F-03: Change password -- backend endpoint `PUT /api/users/me/password` exists but the frontend flow is noted as needing improvement
- F-04: Admin user role editing -- only ban/unban, no role modification UI
- F-06: Admin page tests -- no tests for AdminDashboard, CategoryManage, ContentModeration, UserManage
- F-07: Backend search/category tests -- PostControllerTest/PostServiceTest are missing search and by-category test cases

**Architecture modules not yet started (from `D:/aToys/LargeScale/docs/architecture.md`):**
- Notifications are P1 priority and have been implemented
- No evidence of WebSocket/SSE for real-time notifications (current implementation is polling-based)
- No Docker/containerization
- No CI/CD configuration

**Routing setup (from `D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/App.tsx`):**

The app uses `BrowserRouter` with nested routes. A `Layout` component wraps public-facing pages with Header/Footer. Admin pages use a separate `AdminLayout`.

| `/` | HomePage | No |
| `/login` | LoginPage | No |
| `/register` | RegisterPage | No |

**Notable frontend feature -- Mock mode:**
`D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/api/mockDb.ts` is a comprehensive 875-line client-side mock database that runs in localStorage. When the backend is unreachable (network error), the frontend automatically falls back to mock mode. The mock implements all API endpoints with realistic seed data (4 categories, 8 posts, 9 comments, 3 users, notifications). This allows the frontend to be developed and demonstrated independently of the backend.

**State management:**
- `AuthContext` in `D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx` -- stores user, isAuthenticated, isAdmin in React context + localStorage
- `@tanstack/react-query` -- all server data fetching goes through React Query with centralized query keys (`D:/aToys/LargeScale/frontend/src/lib/queryKeys.ts`)
- JWT tokens stored in localStorage with automatic refresh interceptor in the Axios client

The Layout supports 4 themes (classic blue, warm tea, sakura pink, dark) toggled via a paint-brush button in the Header. Theme classes are applied to the body element.

- `PUT /api/notifications/{id}/read` -- Mark as read

## F-04 Investigation Report: Admin User Role Modification

### Verdict: F-04 is **PARTIALLY COMPLETED** -- the backend is fully implemented, but the frontend has NO UI for role changes.

### 1. Backend Controller (`AdminUserController.java`)

The controller at `D:\aToys\LargeScale\backend\src\main\java\com\cc91\controller\AdminUserController.java` exposes **four endpoints**:

| # | Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|--------|------|---------|
| 1 | `GET` | `/api/admin/users` | Paginated user list (returns `AdminUserDTO`) |
| 2 | `PUT` | `/api/admin/users/{id}/ban` | Ban a user (sets `isLocked=true`, `lockUntil=null`) |
| 3 | `PUT` | `/api/admin/users/{id}/unban` | Unban a user (sets `isLocked=false`, resets failed attempts) |
| 4 | **`PUT`** | **`/api/admin/users/{id}/role`** | **Change user role** (accepts `UpdateUserRoleRequest`, sets `user.setRole(...)`) |

The role-change endpoint (lines 95-109) is fully implemented. It takes an `UpdateUserRoleRequest` body, looks up the user, sets the new role, and saves.

### 2. Backend Service (`UserService.java`)

The file at `D:\aToys\LargeScale\backend\src\main\java\com\cc91\service\UserService.java` does **NOT** contain a `changeRole` method. The role modification in `AdminUserController` is implemented by **directly using `UserRepository`** -- the controller injects `UserRepository` (not `UserService`) and performs the role change inline. This is a minor design concern (logic in controller rather than service layer) but it is functional.

### 3. Backend DTO (`UpdateUserRoleRequest.java`)

The file at `D:\aToys\LargeScale\backend\src\main\java\com\cc91\dto\UpdateUserRoleRequest.java` exists and is properly defined:
- Has a `role` field with `@NotBlank` validation
- Restricted to `USER` or `ADMIN` via `@Pattern(regexp = "^(USER|ADMIN)$")`

The `AdminUserDTO` (at the same DTO package) includes a `role` field, so the role is returned in user listings.

### 4. Frontend API (`frontend/src/api/admin.ts`)

The file at `D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\api\admin.ts` **DOES** include the API function for role changes:

```typescript
// Lines 98-101
export async function adminUpdateUserRole(id: number, role: string): Promise<void> {
  await client.put(`/admin/users/${id}/role`, { role });
}
```

The `AdminUser` interface also includes a `role: string` field (line 10).

### 5. Frontend UI (`frontend/src/pages/admin/UserManage.tsx`)

The file at `D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\pages\admin\UserManage.tsx` has **NO role-change UI**. Specifically:

- The import on line 3 imports only `adminGetUsers`, `adminBanUser`, `adminUnbanUser` -- `adminUpdateUserRole` is **NOT imported**.
- The table displays the current role as a static badge (lines 103-106) -- it is read-only, with no dropdown, select, or button to change it.
- The only actions available per user are "Ban" and "Unban" buttons (lines 122-136).
- There is no mutation, handler, or form element related to role modification anywhere in the component.

---

### Summary Table

| Layer | Role Change Present? | Details |
|-------|---------------------|---------|
| Backend Endpoint | YES | `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/role` -- fully working |
| Backend DTO | YES | `UpdateUserRoleRequest` with validation for USER/ADMIN |
| Backend Service | NO (not needed) | Logic is in controller directly via `UserRepository` |
| Frontend API Function | YES | `adminUpdateUserRole()` exists in `admin.ts` |
| Frontend UI | **NO** | `UserManage.tsx` has no import, no mutation, no dropdown/select for role changes |

### Conclusion

F-04's claim that "Admin can only ban/unban users, no role modification functionality" is **accurate from the user's perspective**. While the backend endpoint and frontend API function are both implemented, the admin UI page (`UserManage.tsx`) does not expose any way to trigger a role change. The `adminUpdateUserRole` function sits unused in `admin.ts`. An admin using the application today can only ban or unban users -- they cannot modify user roles through the interface.

Here is my complete analysis of the test patterns in this codebase.

---

## Frontend Test Patterns

### Test Framework and Tooling

- **Framework**: Vitest (`describe`, `it`, `expect`, `vi` from `'vitest'`)
- **Rendering**: `@testing-library/react` -- `render`, `screen`, `waitFor`
- **User interaction**: `@testing-library/user-event` -- `userEvent.setup()`
- **Routing**: `react-router-dom` -- `MemoryRouter`, `Routes`, `Route`
- **Data fetching**: `@tanstack/react-query` -- `QueryClient`, `QueryClientProvider`

### Test Setup (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\test\setup.ts`)

- Extends Vitest's `expect` with `@testing-library/jest-dom/matchers`
- Provides a custom `MockLocalStorage` class (to avoid Node.js 25+ webstorage conflicts), defined as a writable, configurable property on `globalThis` and `window`
- Runs `cleanup()` and `mockStorage.clear()` in `afterEach`

### Custom Render / Wrapper Utilities (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\test\utils.tsx`)

Three utility functions are provided:

1. **`createTestQueryClient()`** -- creates a `QueryClient` with `retry: false` and `gcTime: 0` (prevents retries and caching in tests)
2. **`renderWithProviders(ui, { route, isAuthenticated })`** -- full custom render that optionally sets localStorage auth tokens, wraps with `QueryClientProvider + AuthProvider + MemoryRouter`
3. **`createWrapper({ route })`** -- returns a wrapper function for use with `render(<Component />, { wrapper: createWrapper() })`
4. **`createSimpleWrapper()`** -- `QueryClientProvider + AuthProvider` only, no Router

### Existing Test Patterns (the actual tests do NOT use `utils.tsx` -- they inline their own wrappers)

Looking at the existing test files (`DashboardPage.test.tsx`, `ProfileEditPage.test.tsx`, `CategoryPage.test.tsx`), each file:

1. **Defines `createWrapper()` inline** inside the `describe` block with its own `QueryClient` instance per call. This avoids React Query cache pollution between tests. The wrapper always includes:
   - `QueryClientProvider` with `retry: false, gcTime: 0`
   - `MemoryRouter` (with `initialEntries` for route-dependent pages)
   - `AuthProvider`

2. **Mocks API modules at the top level** with `vi.mock('../../api/someModule')` -- this auto-mocks all exports. Individual test cases then use `vi.mocked(apiFn).mockResolvedValue(...)` or `mockRejectedValue(...)` to set return values.

3. **Mocks `react-router-dom`** when navigation or params are needed:
   ```ts
   const mockNavigate = vi.fn();
   vi.mock('react-router-dom', async () => ({
     ...(await vi.importActual('react-router-dom')),
     useNavigate: () => mockNavigate,
     useParams: () => ({ id: '1' }),  // when needed
   }));
   ```

4. **Sets localStorage** in `beforeEach`:
   ```ts
   localStorage.setItem('access_token', 'test-token');
   localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify({ username: 'testuser', email: 'test@example.com' }));
   ```

5. **Calls `vi.clearAllMocks()`** and `localStorage.clear()` in `beforeEach`.

### Assertion Patterns

- **Rendering verification**: `await waitFor(() => { expect(screen.getByText('...')).toBeInTheDocument(); })`
- **Loading state**: `expect(screen.getByText('加载中...')).toBeInTheDocument()` (synchronous, before async resolves)
- **Navigation assertions**: `expect(mockNavigate).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/some/path')`
- **Form field values**: `expect(screen.getByLabelText('label')).toHaveValue('value')`
- **Mutation call verification**: `expect(userApi.updateProfile).toHaveBeenCalled()` then inspect `vi.mocked(fn).mock.calls[0][0]` for arguments
- **Button disabled state**: `expect(submitButton).toBeDisabled()`
- **Absence of elements**: `expect(screen.queryByText('...')).not.toBeInTheDocument()`

### How Queries/Mutations are Tested

- **Query (useQuery) tests**: Mock the API function to return data, render the component, use `waitFor` or `findByText` to verify the data appears in the DOM.
- **Mutation (useMutation) tests**: Mock the mutation API function, render, wait for form to load, interact with form elements via `userEvent` (`clear`, `type`, `click`), then assert the API function was called with the correct arguments.
- **Error handling**: Mock API as `mockRejectedValue({ response: { data: { message: '...' } } })`, trigger the action, then assert error message text appears.

---

## Backend Test Patterns

### PostControllerTest (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\backend\src\test\java\com\cc91\controller\PostControllerTest.java`)

**Annotations on the class:**
```java
@SpringBootTest
@ActiveProfiles("test")
@DirtiesContext(classMode = DirtiesContext.ClassMode.AFTER_EACH_TEST_METHOD)
```

**Dependencies injected with `@Autowired`:**
- `WebApplicationContext context` (for MockMvc setup)
- `ObjectMapper objectMapper` (for serializing request bodies)
- `PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder`
- `UserRepository userRepository`
- `PostRepository postRepository`

**MockMvc setup** in `@BeforeEach`:
```java
mockMvc = MockMvcBuilders.webAppContextSetup(context).apply(springSecurity()).build();
```

**Database cleanup** in `@BeforeEach`:
```java
postRepository.deleteAll();
userRepository.deleteAll();
```

**Test method annotations:**
- `@WithMockUser(username = "author")` -- for endpoints requiring authentication
- `@Transactional` -- for tests that modify the database

**Arrange-Act-Assert pattern** in every test:
1. **Arrange**: Create and save `User` and `Post` entities via repositories using `saveAndFlush`
2. **Act**: Call `mockMvc.perform(get/post/put/delete(url))` with `.param()` for query parameters and `.content()` for request body
3. **Assert**: Chain `.andExpect(status().isOk())`, `.andExpect(jsonPath("$.field").value("expected"))`

**Request body format**: Uses Java text blocks for JSON:
```java
String requestBody = """
    {
        "title": "测试标题",
        "content": "测试内容"
    }
    """;
```

**Response assertions**:
- Status: `status().isOk()`, `status().isNotFound()`, `status().isForbidden()`
- JSON body: `jsonPath("$.message").value("...")`, `jsonPath("$.data.title").value("...")`
- Paginated: `jsonPath("$.content").isArray()`, `jsonPath("$.content.length()").value(3)`, `jsonPath("$.totalElements").value(3)`

### PostServiceTest (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\backend\src\test\java\com\cc91\service\PostServiceTest.java`)

**Same class-level annotations**: `@SpringBootTest`, `@ActiveProfiles("test")`, `@DirtiesContext`

**Additional injected dependencies**: `EntityManager entityManager` (for `clear()`/`flush()` to force JPA write-through)

**Test method pattern**:
1. Create and save entities with `userRepository.saveAndFlush(user)` and `postRepository.saveAndFlush(post)`
2. Call the service method directly
3. Assert on the returned `PostResponse` or `Page<PostResponse>` object
4. Optionally verify database state with `postRepository.findById()` after `entityManager.flush(); entityManager.clear();`

- Mutations: `statusMutation` calls `adminUpdatePostStatus`, `deletePostMutation` calls `adminDeletePost`, `deleteCommentMutation` calls `adminDeleteComment`

- Mutations: `banMutation` calls `adminBanUser`, `unbanMutation` calls `adminUnbanUser`

For admin tests, localStorage will need to include admin credentials. Looking at the existing pattern, the wrapper will need `AuthProvider` but the components do not directly check role -- the admin API endpoints are protected at the backend level, not the frontend.

### F-07: Backend Search/By-Category Tests

**PostControllerTest** -- needs tests for two new endpoints:
1. `GET /api/posts/by-category/{categoryId}?page=0&size=10` -- tests needed for: existing category with posts, empty category, non-existent category (404), pagination
2. `GET /api/posts/search?keyword=xxx&page=0&size=10` -- tests needed for: matching results, no results, empty/blank keyword, pagination

**PostServiceTest** -- needs tests for two new service methods:
1. `getPostsByCategory(Long categoryId, int page, int size)` -- must create Category entities (new; existing tests only create User + Post). The Post entity has a `categoryId` field. Tests needed for: valid category with posts, empty category, non-existent category throws `ResourceNotFoundException("版块不存在")`, only returns PUBLISHED posts, pagination, ordering by createdAt DESC
2. `searchPosts(String keyword, int page, int size)` -- tests needed for: matching title, matching content, no results, null/empty keyword returns empty Page, pagination, only searches PUBLISHED posts

Key difference from existing service tests: the `getPostsByCategory` tests require also creating `Category` entities. You will need to inject `CategoryRepository` (or whatever repository manages Category) and save categories before creating posts with `setCategoryId()`.

The Post entity supports `categoryId` via `post.setCategoryId(Long)`. The repository method used is `findByCategoryIdAndStatus(Long categoryId, String status, Pageable pageable)`.

Here is my complete analysis of the test patterns in this codebase.

---

## Frontend Test Patterns

### Test Framework and Tooling

- **Framework**: Vitest (`describe`, `it`, `expect`, `vi` from `'vitest'`)
- **Rendering**: `@testing-library/react` -- `render`, `screen`, `waitFor`
- **User interaction**: `@testing-library/user-event` -- `userEvent.setup()`
- **Routing**: `react-router-dom` -- `MemoryRouter`, `Routes`, `Route`
- **Data fetching**: `@tanstack/react-query` -- `QueryClient`, `QueryClientProvider`

### Test Setup (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\test\setup.ts`)

- Extends Vitest's `expect` with `@testing-library/jest-dom/matchers`
- Provides a custom `MockLocalStorage` class (to avoid Node.js 25+ webstorage conflicts), defined as a writable, configurable property on `globalThis` and `window`
- Runs `cleanup()` and `mockStorage.clear()` in `afterEach`

### Custom Render / Wrapper Utilities (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\test\utils.tsx`)

Three utility functions are provided:

1. **`createTestQueryClient()`** -- creates a `QueryClient` with `retry: false` and `gcTime: 0` (prevents retries and caching in tests)
2. **`renderWithProviders(ui, { route, isAuthenticated })`** -- full custom render that optionally sets localStorage auth tokens, wraps with `QueryClientProvider + AuthProvider + MemoryRouter`
3. **`createWrapper({ route })`** -- returns a wrapper function for use with `render(<Component />, { wrapper: createWrapper() })`
4. **`createSimpleWrapper()`** -- `QueryClientProvider + AuthProvider` only, no Router

### Existing Test Patterns (the actual tests do NOT use `utils.tsx` -- they inline their own wrappers)

Looking at the existing test files (`DashboardPage.test.tsx`, `ProfileEditPage.test.tsx`, `CategoryPage.test.tsx`), each file:

1. **Defines `createWrapper()` inline** inside the `describe` block with its own `QueryClient` instance per call. This avoids React Query cache pollution between tests. The wrapper always includes:
   - `QueryClientProvider` with `retry: false, gcTime: 0`
   - `MemoryRouter` (with `initialEntries` for route-dependent pages)
   - `AuthProvider`

2. **Mocks API modules at the top level** with `vi.mock('../../api/someModule')` -- this auto-mocks all exports. Individual test cases then use `vi.mocked(apiFn).mockResolvedValue(...)` or `mockRejectedValue(...)` to set return values.

3. **Mocks `react-router-dom`** when navigation or params are needed:
   ```ts
   const mockNavigate = vi.fn();
   vi.mock('react-router-dom', async () => ({
     ...(await vi.importActual('react-router-dom')),
     useNavigate: () => mockNavigate,
     useParams: () => ({ id: '1' }),  // when needed
   }));
   ```

4. **Sets localStorage** in `beforeEach`:
   ```ts
   localStorage.setItem('access_token', 'test-token');
   localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify({ username: 'testuser', email: 'test@example.com' }));
   ```

5. **Calls `vi.clearAllMocks()`** and `localStorage.clear()` in `beforeEach`.

### Assertion Patterns

- **Rendering verification**: `await waitFor(() => { expect(screen.getByText('...')).toBeInTheDocument(); })`
- **Loading state**: `expect(screen.getByText('加载中...')).toBeInTheDocument()` (synchronous, before async resolves)
- **Navigation assertions**: `expect(mockNavigate).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/some/path')`
- **Form field values**: `expect(screen.getByLabelText('label')).toHaveValue('value')`
- **Mutation call verification**: `expect(userApi.updateProfile).toHaveBeenCalled()` then inspect `vi.mocked(fn).mock.calls[0][0]` for arguments
- **Button disabled state**: `expect(submitButton).toBeDisabled()`
- **Absence of elements**: `expect(screen.queryByText('...')).not.toBeInTheDocument()`

### How Queries/Mutations are Tested

- **Query (useQuery) tests**: Mock the API function to return data, render the component, use `waitFor` or `findByText` to verify the data appears in the DOM.
- **Mutation (useMutation) tests**: Mock the mutation API function, render, wait for form to load, interact with form elements via `userEvent` (`clear`, `type`, `click`), then assert the API function was called with the correct arguments.
- **Error handling**: Mock API as `mockRejectedValue({ response: { data: { message: '...' } } })`, trigger the action, then assert error message text appears.

---

## Backend Test Patterns

### PostControllerTest (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\backend\src\test\java\com\cc91\controller\PostControllerTest.java`)

**Annotations on the class:**
```java
@SpringBootTest
@ActiveProfiles("test")
@DirtiesContext(classMode = DirtiesContext.ClassMode.AFTER_EACH_TEST_METHOD)
```

**Dependencies injected with `@Autowired`:**
- `WebApplicationContext context` (for MockMvc setup)
- `ObjectMapper objectMapper` (for serializing request bodies)
- `PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder`
- `UserRepository userRepository`
- `PostRepository postRepository`

**MockMvc setup** in `@BeforeEach`:
```java
mockMvc = MockMvcBuilders.webAppContextSetup(context).apply(springSecurity()).build();
```

**Database cleanup** in `@BeforeEach`:
```java
postRepository.deleteAll();
userRepository.deleteAll();
```

**Test method annotations:**
- `@WithMockUser(username = "author")` -- for endpoints requiring authentication
- `@Transactional` -- for tests that modify the database

**Arrange-Act-Assert pattern** in every test:
1. **Arrange**: Create and save `User` and `Post` entities via repositories using `saveAndFlush`
2. **Act**: Call `mockMvc.perform(get/post/put/delete(url))` with `.param()` for query parameters and `.content()` for request body
3. **Assert**: Chain `.andExpect(status().isOk())`, `.andExpect(jsonPath("$.field").value("expected"))`

**Request body format**: Uses Java text blocks for JSON:
```java
String requestBody = """
    {
        "title": "测试标题",
        "content": "测试内容"
    }
    """;
```

**Response assertions**:
- Status: `status().isOk()`, `status().isNotFound()`, `status().isForbidden()`
- JSON body: `jsonPath("$.message").value("...")`, `jsonPath("$.data.title").value("...")`
- Paginated: `jsonPath("$.content").isArray()`, `jsonPath("$.content.length()").value(3)`, `jsonPath("$.totalElements").value(3)`

### PostServiceTest (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\backend\src\test\java\com\cc91\service\PostServiceTest.java`)

**Same class-level annotations**: `@SpringBootTest`, `@ActiveProfiles("test")`, `@DirtiesContext`

**Additional injected dependencies**: `EntityManager entityManager` (for `clear()`/`flush()` to force JPA write-through)

**Test method pattern**:
1. Create and save entities with `userRepository.saveAndFlush(user)` and `postRepository.saveAndFlush(post)`
2. Call the service method directly
3. Assert on the returned `PostResponse` or `Page<PostResponse>` object
4. Optionally verify database state with `postRepository.findById()` after `entityManager.flush(); entityManager.clear();`

---

## What Needs to Be Added

### F-06: Admin Page Frontend Tests

Four components need tests. Here is what each component uses:

**AdminDashboard** (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\pages\admin\AdminDashboard.tsx`):
- Queries: `adminGetUsers` (key: `queryKeys.admin.users()`), `adminGetPosts` (key: `queryKeys.admin.posts()`), `getCategories` (key: `queryKeys.categories.list()`)
- Displays: stat cards (totalUsers, totalPosts, totalCategories, lockedUsers), quick links (Link to admin routes), recent users table
- API modules to mock: `../../api/admin` and `../../api/category`
- No mutations, no router params needed

**CategoryManage** (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\pages\admin\CategoryManage.tsx`):
- Queries: `getCategories` (key: `queryKeys.categories.list()`)
- Mutations: `saveMutation` calls `createCategory` or `updateCategory`, `deleteMutation` calls `deleteCategory`
- Uses `confirm()` dialog for delete
- API modules to mock: `../../api/category`
- Imports from `../../components/ErrorMessage`

**ContentModeration** (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\pages\admin\ContentModeration.tsx`):
- Queries: `adminGetPosts` (enabled when tab=posts), `adminGetComments` (enabled when tab=comments)
- Mutations: `statusMutation` calls `adminUpdatePostStatus`, `deletePostMutation` calls `adminDeletePost`, `deleteCommentMutation` calls `adminDeleteComment`
- Tab switching between 'posts' and 'comments', status filter buttons
- API modules to mock: `../../api/admin`

**UserManage** (`D:\aToys\LargeScale\frontend\src\pages\admin\UserManage.tsx`):
- Queries: `adminGetUsers` (key: `queryKeys.admin.users()`)
- Mutations: `banMutation` calls `adminBanUser`, `unbanMutation` calls `adminUnbanUser`
- Uses `confirm()` dialog for ban
- API modules to mock: `../../api/admin`

For admin tests, localStorage will need to include admin credentials. Looking at the existing pattern, the wrapper will need `AuthProvider` but the components do not directly check role -- the admin API endpoints are protected at the backend level, not the frontend.

### F-07: Backend Search/By-Category Tests

**PostControllerTest** -- needs tests for two new endpoints:
1. `GET /api/posts/by-category/{categoryId}?page=0&size=10` -- tests needed for: existing category with posts, empty category, non-existent category (404), pagination
2. `GET /api/posts/search?keyword=xxx&page=0&size=10` -- tests needed for: matching results, no results, empty/blank keyword, pagination

The Post entity supports `categoryId` via `post.setCategoryId(Long)`. The repository method used is `findByCategoryIdAndStatus(Long categoryId, String status, Pageable pageable)`.

1	# CC91 论坛系统 - Lead 工作协议
2	
3	你是 CC91 论坛项目的 Lead，直接管理 developer 和 qa，对需求交付质量与节奏负责。
4	
5	## 团队
6	
7	| 角色 | 何时启动 | Spawn 参数（subagent） | 核心职责 |
8	|------|---------|----------------------|---------|
9	| developer | 进入开发阶段后立即启动 | name: developer（agentName: "developer"） | 实现代码、补充测试、修复构建问题 |
10	| qa | 开发完成且可运行后启动 | name: qa（agentName: "qa"） | 执行测试、验证回归、输出测试报告 |
11	
12	## 统一任务规范
13	
14	每个任务都要有唯一 ID，并维护状态流转：`not-started` -> `in-progress` -> `completed`。
15	
16	阻塞表达约定：不新增 `blocked` 状态。任务一旦开始执行即保持为 `in-progress`；若因依赖、环境、外部输入等原因无法继续推进，必须在任务记录中显式补充阻塞字段。
17	
18	每个任务至少包含：
19	- 背景与目标（要解决什么问题）
20	- 实现范围（明确改哪些模块）
21	- 验收标准（功能、测试、边界）
22	- 依赖关系（阻塞来源、被阻塞对象，以及阻塞记录）
23	
24	阻塞记录至少包含：
25	- blocker：阻塞原因
26	- blocked-by：具体阻塞来源（任务、人员、系统、环境）
27	- blocked-at：开始阻塞时间
28	- next-action：解除阻塞所需动作与负责人
29	- escalation-owner / escalation-at：升级责任人与升级时间
30	
31	## 工作流
32	
33	### Phase 1: 理解与规划
34	
35	目标：把需求转化为可执行任务，并明确风险与边界。
36	
37	输入：用户需求、现有代码上下文。
38	
39	执行步骤：
40	1. 与用户澄清业务目标、范围、非目标、约束。
41	2. 拆分任务并建立依赖顺序。
42	3. 标记高风险项（兼容性、数据安全、性能、迁移影响）。
43	
44	产出：结构化任务清单（含依赖、优先级、验收标准）。
45	
46	完成标准：任务无歧义、依赖清晰、可直接进入开发。
47	
48	### Phase 2: 开发
49	
50	目标：按任务清单实现功能并保持可构建、可测试状态。
51	
52	输入：已确认任务清单。
53	
54	执行步骤：
55	1. Spawn developer，按任务 ID 分派实现工作。
56	2. 每个任务必须附带验收标准模板（见下文）。
57	3. 持续跟踪状态与阻塞，必要时拆分子任务。
58	
59	产出：代码变更、对应测试、实现说明。
60	
61	完成标准：功能实现完成，相关测试已补齐并可执行。
62	
63	### Phase 3: 测试
64	
65	目标：验证功能正确性与回归稳定性。
66	
67	输入：开发完成的代码与测试计划。
68	
69	执行步骤：
70	1. Spawn qa，分配测试任务与回归范围。
71	2. qa 必须实际运行测试，不接受仅静态分析结论。
72	3. 输出测试报告：通过项、失败项、复现步骤、环境信息。
73	
74	产出：测试报告与缺陷列表。
75	
76	完成标准：关键路径通过；失败项已有修复或明确处置结论。
77	
78	### Phase 4: 审查
79	
80	目标：在合并前兜底质量与风险。
81	
82	输入：代码变更与测试报告。
83	
84	执行步骤：
85	1. 按审查清单执行安全性、API、错误处理、代码质量检查。
86	2. 对发现问题分类：阻断问题（必须修）与建议优化（可后续）。
87	3. 阻断问题直接修复或退回 developer 处理。
88	
89	产出：审查结论（通过/退回）与问题记录。
90	
91	完成标准：无阻断问题，变更可进入收尾。
92	
93	### Phase 5: 收尾
94	
95	目标：形成可追踪、可回滚、可复盘的交付闭环。
96	
97	输入：通过审查的最终变更。
98	
99	执行步骤：
100	1. 确认任务状态全部为 completed。
101	2. 提交前检查改动范围与提交信息。
102	3. 完成 git 提交并记录交付摘要。
103	
104	产出：规范提交记录与交付说明。
105	
106	完成标准：代码已提交、说明完整、可回溯。
107	
108	## 验收标准模板（分配给 developer/qa 时必须包含）
109	
110	- 功能验收：给出可观察行为和输入输出。
111	- 测试验收：需执行的测试类型与最小覆盖范围。
112	- 边界验收：异常输入、空值、权限、并发等边界场景。
113	- 回归范围：受影响模块与重点回归路径。
114	
115	## 阻塞与升级机制
116	
117	- 任一任务阻塞超过 30 分钟，必须上报阻塞原因与已尝试方案。
118	- 阻塞超过 2 次未解决，Lead 必须调整拆分策略或变更实现路径。
119	- 若涉及需求歧义，优先回到 Phase 1 与用户重新确认。
120	
121	## 提交规范
122	
123	提交应小步、聚焦、可回滚，避免将无关改动混入同一次提交。
124	
125	推荐格式：
126	```bash
127	git add <具体文件>
128	git commit -m "<type>: <简要描述>"
129	```
130	
131	`type` 建议：`feat`、`fix`、`refactor`、`test`、`docs`、`chore`。
132	
133	## 审查清单
134	
135	- [ ] 安全性：是否完成输入验证、认证授权、敏感数据保护
136	- [ ] API 设计：是否符合 RESTful 规范、错误码与错误体是否一致
137	- [ ] 错误处理：是否覆盖边界条件与异常路径，是否避免吞异常
138	- [ ] 代码质量：命名是否清晰、结构是否合理、是否存在重复逻辑
139	- [ ] 测试质量：是否包含新增逻辑的正向与异常用例
140	
141	## 问题跟踪
142	
143	- 审查代码、与用户对话、或任何环节中发现 Bug / 未完成功能时，**必须立即写入 `docs/issues.md`**
144	- 格式：按现有条目样式，标注优先级（P0/P1/P2）和状态 `[ ]`
145	- **修复后立即从文件中删除该条目**，不保留 `[x] 已修复` 的条目
146	- `docs/issues.md` 只保留未完成的工作，保持简洁
147	
148	## 提交流程
149	
150	当用户要求提交，或一个完整功能/修复批次完成后：
151	
152	1. **创建分支** — 从 develop 创建功能分支
153	   ```bash
154	   git checkout develop
155	   git pull origin develop
156	   git checkout -b feat/功能描述
157	   ```
158	
159	2. **分类暂存并提交** — 按逻辑分组，使用 conventional commits：
160	   - `feat: 新功能描述`
161	   - `fix: 修复描述`
162	   - `refactor: 重构描述`
163	   - `test: 测试描述`
164	   - `docs: 文档描述`
165	
166	3. **推送并创建 PR** — 目标分支为 develop
167	   ```bash
168	   git push -u origin feat/功能描述
169	   gh pr create --base develop --title "标题" --body "描述"
170	   ```
171	
172	4. **验证** — 确认 PR 创建成功，等待合并
173	
174	## 技术栈
175	
176	- 后端: Spring Boot 3.2 + Maven + MySQL + Flyway
177	- 前端: React 19 + Vite + TypeScript + react-router-dom + axios
178	- 测试: JUnit 5 + MockMvc (后端), Vitest + RTL (前端)

`high effort → 3+4 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle, up to 6 each)

Run **7 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Name the cheaper alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

Cleanup and altitude candidates use the same `file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in
`failure_scenario`, state the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank
cleanup and altitude findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

管理员开始修改用户 A 的角色 → 表格中 50 个下拉框全部冻结 → 如果请求挂起，管理员无法修改任何其他用户的角色，直到超时。
使用行级 loading 状态（如 Map<userId, boolean>）代替全局 isPending，或在接受此限制的情况下在 UI 上给出明确提示。
#9 MAINTBackend hibernate.dialect 强制 H2Dialect 掩盖了 MySQL/H2 语法不兼容
文件 application-test.yml:11

为让搜索测试通过，添加了 hibernate.dialect: org.hibernate.dialect.H2Dialect。H2 使用自己的 SQL 解析器（即使开了 MODE=MySQL），这意味着使用 MySQL 特有语法的查询在测试中可以通过，但在生产中会失败。

新增 Repository 方法使用了 MySQL 的 GROUP_CONCAT 或 FULL OUTER JOIN → 测试在 H2 上通过 → 生产环境查询报语法错误。
根本原因是 Spring Data JPA 的 Containing 方法生成的 LIKE ESCAPE '\\' 语法不被 H2 默认接受。考虑在测试中使用 MODE=MySQL + 正确的 H2 兼容配置，而非覆盖 dialect。长期建议引入 Testcontainers + MySQL 做集成测试。

content.text:
两种测试方式，取决于你本地有没有 MySQL：

## 方式 A：前端独立测试（无需后端，推荐）

项目内置了 Mock 模式，后端不可用时自动切换到本地模拟数据。

```bash
cd frontend && npm run dev
```

然后浏览器打开 http://localhost:5173 ，按以下步骤测试：

### 1. 修改密码页面 (F-03)

| 步骤 | 操作 | 预期结果 |
|------|------|----------|
| 1 | 点右上角登录（Mock 模式下随便输入即可进入） | 进入 Dashboard |
| 2 | 在快捷卡片中找到 **"修改密码"** 卡片，点击 | 跳转到 `/dashboard/password` |
| 3 | 旧密码随便填，新密码填 `abc`（少于 6 位），点确认 | 红色提示 "新密码长度不能少于 6 位" |
| 4 | 新密码和确认密码填不一致的值，点确认 | 红色提示 "两次输入的新密码不一致" |
| 5 | 三个字段都填合法值，点确认 | 自动跳转回 Dashboard（不再停在原页面） |

### 2. 管理员角色修改 (F-04)

| 步骤 | 操作 | 预期结果 |
|------|------|----------|
| 1 | 用管理员账号登录，进入 **管理后台 → 用户管理** | 看到用户列表，角色列显示为下拉框 |
| 2 | 点击某个用户的角色下拉框，重新选择当前角色（比如 USER 选 USER） | 无反应，不弹确认框（重复选择保护） |
| 3 | 选择不同角色（如 USER → ADMIN） | 弹出确认对话框 "确定要修改角色吗？" |
| 4 | 点取消 | 下拉框恢复原值 |
| 5 | 找到管理员自己的那一行，尝试修改角色 | 弹出特别警告 "警告：修改自己的角色可能导致您失去管理权限" |

### 3. 自动化测试（已全部通过）

```bash
# 前端测试
cd frontend && npx vitest run

# 后端测试
cd backend && mvn test
```

## 方式 B：前后端联调（需要 MySQL）

如果你本地有 MySQL 8.0+：

```bash
# 1. 配置数据库
cp .env.example .env
# 编辑 .env 填入数据库密码

# 2. 启动后端（Flyway 自动建表）
cd backend && mvn spring-boot:run

# 3. 启动前端（另开终端）
cd frontend && npm run dev
```

后端启动后 Mock 模式会自动关闭，所有操作走真实 API。

not the test suite, not an `import` of an internal function and a
`console.log`. The app as a user (human or programmatic) would meet
it: the CLI at its command, the server at its socket, the GUI at its

A project skill that launches this app is the repo's verified path —
its author already cold-started from a Linux container and committed

driver. Use it instead of rediscovering.

## Otherwise: match the shape, use the pattern

Pick the row closest to your project. Each example walks through
launch + first interaction; ignore any trailing "write the skill"
section — you're using the recipe, not authoring one.

| Project type | Handle | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CLI tool | direct invocation, exit code, stdin/stdout | [examples/cli.md](examples/cli.md) |
| Web server / API | background launch + `curl` smoke | [examples/server.md](examples/server.md) |
| TUI / interactive terminal | tmux `send-keys` / `capture-pane` | [examples/tui.md](examples/tui.md) |

If nothing fits, start from the closest match and adapt. For a web

`chromium-cli`, no custom driver needed. For a desktop app,
[examples/electron.md](examples/electron.md) — it has the `_electron`

## Drive it, don't just launch it

Launching with no interaction proves the entrypoint resolves. That's
not running the app — it's typechecking with extra steps. Drive it to

- CLI → type a representative command, check the exit code and output.

skills.name: code-review
skills.content:
`high effort → 3+4 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle, up to 6 each)

Run **7 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Name the cheaper alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

Cleanup and altitude candidates use the same `file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in
`failure_scenario`, state the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank
cleanup and altitude findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
